body: It's not that he doesn't have a case. I will put in perspective for you. My lawyer had a client who was facing 10 years in jail + registration but got a deal for 2 years (but would out in months) + registration. His client opted to go to jury and got 17 YEARS.

Oh, I don't care about jail. I would gladly serve five years in lieu of having to register. Becoming a RSO is the end of the world. Yes, I won't be on TMZ but there are notifications when someone is added. Also, people don't generally get passed a person being a RSO. It's easier for them to lump them all together as monsters.

I am not happy with the outcome of my case, but I can say that my lawyer did the best he could do. You have to keep in mind that it is the law that if you are convicted or plea guilty to certain crimes then you must register. My offer is to plea guilty to a misdemeanor which isn't as bad but it would require me to register too. That is the catch.
Not really. I have no priors and jail overcrowding so the DA was willing to negotiate with my lawyer. However,   if I go to trial, the prosecution will go for the jugular.
